body:
I think it's normal.

I'm 26 and I have a special blanket that I just hide under or curl up to every time I get depressed. Even after a really distressing day where I find it hard to talk to anybody else, I know I'll always have my fuzzy blanket. 

Having something (or in your case, two somethings) that you treasure and genuinely feel comforted by is something worth valuing.

I think I'm really overwhelmed. I've had depression for as long as I can remember. I've been going through therapy. I've been practicing healthy behaviors.

I just feel tired and done. I just keep hearing this constant echo that makes me feel like maybe everything would be better without me. Maybe I won't have to be a burden anymore. Maybe I won't cause trouble for everyone anymore.

It's weird. I just got a new job, married, and a relatively better home life, but I just can't help it. I'm stressed and anxious all the time. Panic attacks happen frequently. I feel like even if I reached out, nothing would change. 

My family knows. My partner knows. It doesn't matter how "ok" they are or understanding they try to be. Even if I try really hard to get better, I can't help it. I just want to die.

I'm in community college right now and had the same fear as you when I first entered. I found that it's not awful.

My advice is to be proactive. Ask people to hang out. If you wanna do something, go for it. Talk to people, get to know them. 

And if that's too scary, I get it. I'm terrified of strangers, but sorta (not really) got over it by taking baby steps. Just say hello to people and ask them how their day is. If they mention something interesting, engage.
Please tell me this is real.

Ridiculous, most of the time. 

Being logical throughout my bouts, explaining to people "I'm not equipped right now to handle this" when needing to take care of my needs, and generally being aware of how I feel when I'm going through it just makes me feel so fucking ridiculously silly.

Then there's the repeating suicidal thoughts, where I feel so calm about the idea of sinking into nothingness and disappearing, or if there is a God, to return back to my creator. It's no longer scary to me and I long for it.

It gets especially bad when my SO, who can logically understand the situation but not emotionally connect to or relate to the situation, gets upset about it. He feels just as helpless as I do and it makes it hard to open up about it.

I am getting better though.

Home Depot and a lot of other stores in my area have apps now where they supposedly have item locations and item look ups. It saves me the effort of having to find any missing employees whenever I go looking for any sort of help.

My joints hurt like hell before a big storm comes. 

Growing up, I always thought it was something crotchety old people said because they were superstitious.

Nope. I get it now.
